MTN Nigeria has deployed 106 new network sites and upgraded 97 existing ones across the country to improve connectivity and address growing demand for mobile services. The latest rollout brings the number of new and upgraded sites to 203, covering selected locations across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones and the Federal Capital Territory, according to a statement on Sunday. The investment spans 2G, 3G and 4G technologies as the telecommunications operator seeks to strengthen network capacity and improve service delivery amid increasing data consumption and reliance on digital services. In the South-West, the deployment includes four new sites and 16 upgrades in Lagos, two new sites and three upgrades in Ogun, alongside additional upgrades in Ondo, Ekiti, Osun and Oyo states. In the South-East, Anambra received one new site and one upgrade, while Abia got two new sites and Imo one upgrade. Ebonyi recorded six new sites and four upgrades. Across the North-Central, seven new sites and four upgrades were deployed in Benue, eight new sites and four upgrades in Kogi, and one new site in Kwara. The Federal Capital Territory also received nine new sites. In the North-East, the programme includes six new sites and two upgrades in Bauchi, two new sites and four upgrades in Borno, five new sites in Gombe, one new site and two upgrades in Taraba, five new sites in Yobe, and two upgrades in Adamawa. The company said the expansion was aimed at addressing increasing network usage, improving service quality and meeting the changing connectivity needs of customers. While the new sites are expected to extend network infrastructure into selected locations, upgrades to existing facilities will strengthen capacity in areas experiencing increased usage. Commenting on the investment, Karl Toriola, Chief Executive Officer of MTN Nigeria, said, “Reliable connectivity is central to how Nigerians live, work and do business. Our continued network investment reflects our commitment to keeping pace with growing demand, addressing congestion and delivering a dependable experience for our customers. “Through this 203-site rollout, we are strengthening capacity in busy commercial centres and university communities while extending coverage to underserved areas. This goes beyond infrastructure alone; it includes connecting people to opportunities and enabling them to participate more fully in the digital economy. Through our ‘Live It 100’ promise, we remain committed to making connectivity accessible to more Nigerians.” Justice Okamgba Justice has over three years experience spanning digital and print media.
